## A deterministic, frame-based cooperative coroutine scheduler.
## All timing is driven solely by advance() — byte-for-byte reproducible.
extends RefCounted
class_name FrameScheduler


## The current simulated frame (starts at 0 before the first advance).
var current_frame: int = 0


# State for each pending task: { id, name, on_complete, state, wait_type, ... }
var _tasks: Dictionary = {}
var _next_id: int = 0
var _current_running_id: int = -1

# A persistent signal used only to suspend a coroutine inside the helper
# methods; none of the task coroutines ever await this in a way that needs
# an emission, so we don't emit it. We drive resumption via GDScriptFunctionState.resume()
# directly (or signal emission for wait_signal).
var _suspend_signal: Signal = Signal()


func _init() -> void:
    var emitter := Object.new()
    emitter.add_user_signal("suspend")
    _suspend_signal = emitter.connect.get_signal("suspend")


## Registers and starts a task. Tasks are assigned integer ids in spawn
## order, starting at 0. The body runs synchronously until its first
## suspension or completion. When it returns, on_complete is called once.
func spawn(task_name: String, body: Callable, on_complete: Callable = Callable()) -> void:
    var id := _next_id
    _next_id += 1

    # Stub the task so the body's first wait-helper sees its assigned id.
    var t := {
        "id": id,
        "name": task_name,
        "on_complete": on_complete,
        "state": null,
        "wait_type": null,
        "completed": false,
    }
    _tasks[id] = t
    _current_running_id = id

    var state: GDScriptFunctionState = body.call()
    t["state"] = state
    _current_running_id = -1

    if not state.is_valid():
        _invoke_complete(id)


## Coroutine helper: suspend the calling task for exactly n frames (n >= 1).
func wait_frames(n: int) -> void:
    assert(n >= 1)
    var id := _current_running_id
    var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
    t["wait_type"] = "frames"
    t["ready_frame"] = current_frame + n
    _suspend_task(id)


## Coroutine helper: suspend until cond.call() returns true.
func wait_until(cond: Callable) -> void:
    var id := _current_running_id
    var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
    t["wait_type"] = "until"
    t["cond"] = cond
    _suspend_task(id)


## Coroutine helper: suspend until sig is emitted; ready on the frame the
## emission occurs (only emissions after the wait began count).
func wait_signal(sig: Signal) -> void:
    var id := _current_running_id
    var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
    t["wait_type"] = "signal"
    t["signal"] = sig
    t["signal_emitted"] = false
    # Connect the signal so we spot emissions occurring after the wait began.
    # The bound id ensures the handler only affects this specific task.
    var handler: Callable = Callable(self, "_on_signal_emitted").bind(id)
    sig.connect(handler)
    t["signal_handler"] = handler
    _suspend_task(id)


## Advance the simulation by frames. Each frame: increment current_frame,
## then consider every not-yet-finished suspended task exactly once in
## ascending task-id order. If ready, it resumes synchronously until its
## next suspension or completion.
func advance(frames: int) -> void:
    assert(frames >= 0)
    for _f in range(frames):
        current_frame += 1
        var ids: Array = _tasks.keys()
        ids.sort()
        for id in ids:
            # Re-fetch: a prior task in the same frame might have completed this one.
            if not _tasks.has(id):
                continue
            var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
            if _is_ready(t):
                _resume_task(id)


func _is_ready(t: Dictionary) -> bool:
    match t["wait_type"]:
        "frames":
            return current_frame >= t["ready_frame"]
        "until":
            return t["cond"].call()
        "signal":
            return t["signal_emitted"]
    return false


func _resume_task(id: int) -> void:
    var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
    # Signal-waiters are now ready; disconnect their handler so late emissions
    # don't trigger (and so handler removal is deterministic).
    if t.get("wait_type") == "signal":
        var sig: Signal = t["signal"]
        var handler: Callable = t["signal_handler"]
        if sig.is_connected(handler):
            sig.disconnect(handler)
    t.erase("signal_handler")

    _current_running_id = id
    # Resume the coroutine from its last suspension point. Because resume()
    # is called without arguments, the expression the coroutine was awaiting
    # (the dummy _suspend_signal) evaluates to null, and execution proceeds
    # to the next line in the coroutine body.
    var state: GDScriptFunctionState = t["state"]
    state.resume()
    _current_running_id = -1

    if not state.is_valid():
        _invoke_complete(id)


func _suspend_task(id: int) -> void:
    # Suspend this coroutine and return control to the caller (spawn/advance).
    # The coroutine pauses at this await; it will be re-entered later by
    # state.resume(), which clears the await and proceeds.
    await _suspend_signal


func _on_signal_emitted(id: int) -> void:
    if _tasks.has(id):
        var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
        if t.get("wait_type") == "signal":
            t["signal_emitted"] = true


func _invoke_complete(id: int) -> void:
    if not _tasks.has(id):
        return
    var t: Dictionary = _tasks[id]
    if t["completed"]:
        return
    t["completed"] = true
    _tasks.erase(id)
    var on_complete: Callable = t["on_complete"]
    if on_complete.is_valid():
        on_complete.call(t["name"])
